Half resolution should be default IMO

> Half resolution should be default IMO

Keep in mind this setting also affects VoxelGI rendering, so if we change it, this will also affect existing projects using VoxelGI. To avoid this, we could enable half-resolution GI for new projects only (similar to multi-bounce AO).

However, in the age of upscaling, half-resolution GI isn't as desirable since you'll often decrease the entire 3D rendering resolution to something lower than native. If you do so, you generally don't want half-resolution GI as it'll become really low-resolution (e.g. if using FSR2 Performance on 2160p, half-resolution GI would be 540p).

Are dynamic objects supported? Specifically, do they affect global illumination and appear in reflections?

> After your push, I'm noticing light leaking again. Everything is set to default. I reproduced this in your sponza project and found that the leakage primarily stems from the voxel size at that distance—the voxels jumps to the third cascade with default settings, ignoring structures that aren't thick enough to be fully covered. **Two ways to improve accuracy:** - **Decrease cell size** (and increase cascade count) — this gives finer resolution. - **Increase the `Cascades Forward Offset`** — this shifts cascade boundaries to capture more geometry. See the comparisons below. --- If the previous version showed no leakage, the change may be due to me setting `rendering/global_illumination/hddagi/screen_probe_directional_adaptive` from `true` to `false` by default. That setting subdivides screen probes for higher accuracy. I disabled it by default because it increases GPU time and isn't really necessary for all scenes. --- Default settings (Cell Size = 0.2) — leaks visible
--- Cell Size = 0.03 with 5 cascades — no leakage
--- Default Cell Size = 0.2 + Cascades Forward Offset = 0.3 — no leakage

@David-Zuloyan I just made a rough prototype of dynamic objects on hdda gi, the scene is totally luminated by gi without lights.
Mesh instances with "object level cache" toggled will hold a unique voxel cache representation the detailed surface and records radiosity, basically same as what the global one does. 

It does increase the overhead by about 20% in my experiment, as we have to add additional trace between screen trace and global trace, and allocate extra storage for this. So it's just a proof of concept, I'm not going to add this before other parts were done. Maybe in another proposal or PR.
